integrity: For a labeling with alpha positive vertices on the A-side and beta on the B-side, choose the smallest zero B-index and the largest zero A-index. Their defenders see every zero on the opposite side, yielding the exact lower bound alpha+ceil((n-beta)/2)+beta+ceil((n-alpha)/2). Minimizing this discrete expression gives n+1 for odd n and n+2 for even n. The two universal endpoints attain the bound. In odd order equality forces one positive vertex on each side, and the nesting then forces those vertices to be a_1 and b_n. An explicit second optimum proves nonuniqueness in every even order.
scientific_limitations: All minimum functions are classified only for odd n; the even case is proved nonunique but not fully enumerated.
Finite verification covers n from three through seven and is corroborative only.
A differently phrased or non-indexed half-graph specialization may exist.
title: Strong Roman domination of half graphs
